P001.text: Treat each new account’s path to its first published schedule as a history requiring traceable continuity across people, preparation steps and schedule versions. Account creation, invitations, draft saves and publication are documented event types; offline preparation is unobserved. Whether responsibility actually passes between people, which team information is required and when the account intends to publish remain questions to establish, not supplied facts.

P002.text: For a bounded cohort of new accounts, link existing events using account and schedule identifiers, checking that drafts and publications refer to the same schedule lineage.

P003.text: Record each relevant handling or handoff event with the responsible role, time, purpose, information or version passed, and intended next step.

P004.text: Use brief customer follow-ups to document offline preparation and intended roster timing, labeling retrospective reports and unknowns explicitly.

P005.text: Inspect histories for continuity, conflicting identities or versions, and unexplained transitions; ask the relevant participant to clarify gaps without replacing the original record.

P006.text: Use the eight interviews to suggest checks, not to establish prevalence.

P007.text: Spend the small release slot on one narrow change only if corroborated histories identify a recurring, actionable handoff problem—for example, an explicit missing-information checklist if that problem is confirmed.

P008.text: If histories remain unreliable or reveal no recurring actionable problem, stop short of selecting a presumed friction fix and use the slot to improve the deficient recording step.

P009.text: Before release, define eligible accounts, a common observation window covering their intended roster opportunity, first-publication outcome and recording checks.

P010.text: If feasible, randomly assign eligible accounts to the change or current flow; otherwise use a comparable contemporaneous cohort and document assignment differences.

P011.text: Follow unresolved histories through the agreed window and report accounts whose publication opportunity has not yet occurred separately.

P012.text: Look for an internally consistent sequence connecting account creation, responsible participants, preparation, invitations, draft versions and publication, with reported offline activity distinguished from logged events.

P013.text: Record missing links and contradictions as breaks in documented continuity.

P014.text: A documented wait until a stated roster date is an explained interval; silence alone is not evidence of postponement.

P015.text: After release, observe both whether the targeted handoff becomes more consistently accounted for and whether the proportion reaching a traceable first publication within the predefined window changes.

P016.text: These are proposed observations, not completed findings.

P017.text: A continuous history supports the claim that the examined publication belongs to the tracked account and schedule lineage and that its documented handling is accounted for.

P018.text: Corroborated histories may locate a recurring handoff suitable for the limited release; a gap initially warrants clarification or better recording, not attribution of a customer failure.

P019.text: Improved continuity supports better traceability, while increased first publication is a separate outcome.

P020.text: With valid random assignment, comparable follow-up and reliable outcome capture, a publication difference can support an effect of the change; without those conditions, treat the difference as an association and use clarified histories to guide further testing.

P021.text: Complete histories do not prove truthful reporting, correct identity linkage or absence of unrecorded offline work.

P022.text: Missing events do not prove abandonment, missing preparation or mishandling.

P023.text: The eight interviews cannot establish how common any explanation is.

P024.text: Intended roster dates may change, and accounts still awaiting their publication opportunity cannot yet establish failure to publish.

P025.text: Recording changes can create apparent improvement without changing customer behavior; verify linkage and capture comparability before interpreting results.

P026.text: Small cohorts, incomplete follow-up, differences between comparison groups and concurrent changes can leave the release effect uncertain.

P027.text: If these checks fail or evidence is too sparse, stop causal interpretation, retain the uncertainty and continue targeted follow-up or observation before deciding on another product change.
